findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn processes, so hung flushers are never killed
findings.body: The processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess` directly and is not a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (that is `context.Process`). The new `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard around `process.kill()` is therefore always False in production, and the kill never runs. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. When the cause is `hang`, the stuck process is now left running and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second flusher for the same shards. Two flushers then consume and produce the same segments concurrently, and every further restart leaks one more process. Use `hasattr(process, 'kill')` or check `multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess`/`SpawnProcess` instead.

findings.title: join() never terminates spawned processes, and its deadline break skips cleanup for the rest
findings.body: Two problems in `join()`. First, `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False for `SpawnProcess`, so `process.terminate()` never runs for real flusher processes. Second, the new `if remaining_time <= 0: break` leaves the loop before reaching terminate for the current and all remaining processes. If the deadline expires while waiting on an early process, the later processes are neither waited on nor terminated. Terminate should run for every process regardless of the deadline, and the type check needs to match `SpawnProcess`.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) added to de-flake test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test starts with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which replaces `time.sleep` globally. The new `time.sleep(0.1)`, commented "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change", therefore does nothing. `step.join()` sets `stopped` immediately, and the flusher thread can exit its `while not stopped.value` loop before it flushes. The `(msg,) = messages` assertion can then fail intermittently. Wait on a condition (poll until `messages` is non-empty, with a timeout) or use the real sleep (`monkeypatch.undo()` or a saved reference) for this wait.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard`
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` and the unhealthy metric all use `shard`. This makes dashboards and queries that group by shard inconsistent. In addition, `shard` carries a comma-joined list of shards in `main` but a single shard id in `_ensure_processes_alive`, so one tag key has two different value shapes.

findings.title: Memory info is polled once per per-process buffer on every submit
findings.body: `submit()` now loops over every per-process `SpansBuffer` and extends `memory_infos` with `buffer.get_memory_info()` for each one. That method appears to report on the whole Redis cluster rather than just the buffer's shards. If so, each submit issues N times the INFO calls, and `used` and `available` are both inflated by N. The ratio stays the same, so the result is correct but wasteful. The same applies to `record_stored_segments` per buffer. Query memory once, from a single buffer.
